distinction: These 225 explicit component acceptance tests are a subset of the wider 1,517 tracked specification and acceptance entries. All unexecuted checks are NOT_TESTED.

tests.text: Inspect server HTML in both locales: document language, title, main landmark and headings are correct before scripts run.
Disable JavaScript and open every route family: useful content and navigation remain available.
At 320 px and 400% zoom, no non-exempt page region requires horizontal scrolling.
In both themes, the first keyboard Tab reveals the skip link and Enter reaches main content.
Compare the published SVG checksum with the preserved approved asset.
Test 1x/2x rendering and keyboard focus at 320, 390, 1024 and 1440 px.
Block the logo request: company identity and the home destination remain understandable.
Screen-reader output announces one clear home link, not duplicate brand names.
From a new page load, first Tab exposes the control completely.
Enter moves the screen-reader/keyboard position to main content.
The control remains readable in dark mode, forced colors and 200% text enlargement.
At 1199 and 1200 px, the header changes mode without clipped navigation or a sudden horizontal scrollbar.
At 200% zoom, no destination or language action is lost.
Focus remains visible when tabbing to links after scrolling down the page.
Header does not cover an anchored section heading or form error.
Activate every item in both locales and check final URL and localized page title.
The current destination remains identifiable in a grayscale screenshot.
Open each link in a new tab using normal browser behavior.
At 320 px the full control and the preserved logo fit without overlap.
Button name and expanded state are announced correctly.
When the menu closes, focus returns to the same trigger.
With JavaScript disabled, the navigation destinations remain available.
Keyboard focus cannot escape into covered page content while the sheet is open.
Escape, Close, link activation and browser Back each leave a usable page state.
At landscape 667 by 375 px all menu content can be reached by scrolling.
At reduced motion the sheet appears without translation.
Switch from every service page and confirm the same service remains selected.
Inspect initial HTML for the correct language and localized metadata.
Enter a sample message, switch language and verify that data is preserved or a clear confirmation protects it.
Screen-reader pronunciation follows the actual page language.
System mode follows a device preference change; explicit Light/Dark does not.
Blocked localStorage produces no uncaught error or blank page.
Radio group works with keyboard arrows and has a readable group label.
Theme change preserves form data, route and scroll position.
The trail matches route hierarchy in both languages.
At 320 px all breadcrumb text remains reachable and does not overlap the H1.
Screen-reader output announces a breadcrumb navigation region without reading decorative separators.
Read the hero with video blocked, reduced motion enabled and JavaScript disabled.
Verify exact headline spelling, typography and approved line breaks in FI and EN.
At 200% text enlargement, copy and actions remain inside an expanded panel.
Measure text contrast on the opaque panel rather than a convenient video frame.
Compare representative source and delivery frames for crop, color and compression.
Observe real playback through advancing currentTime on supported desktop and mobile browsers.
Block media downloads and confirm the poster geometry and main journey remain intact.
Reduced-motion first load makes no automatic MP4 request.
Pause stops actual playback and it stays paused after scrolling away and back.
A rejected play promise leaves an accurate Play action, not a false playing state.
Control works by touch and keyboard at every breakpoint.
Screen-reader name describes the next action correctly after each state change.
Both actions work with scripts disabled and normal new-tab behavior.
The secondary destination is visually and programmatically different from an in-page scroll action.
At 320 px and 200% text size, labels are complete and controls remain separate.
All text/background pairs pass the contrast register at default, hover and pressed states.
Tab, Enter and Space follow native semantics; navigation links still open in new tabs.
Repeated activation during busy state produces one operation.
The button remains readable with forced colors and custom text spacing.
At rest, a visitor can distinguish primary, secondary and utility roles without reading documentation.
High-contrast mode preserves the clickable boundary and focus indicator.
Both localized labels fit without artificially reducing type size.
Links remain identifiable in grayscale and without hover.
Keyboard focus is visible across wrapped inline text.
All external and mail links resolve to the intended verified destination.
A screen reader announces purpose without relying on the surrounding visual.
Touch activation works at the edges of the intended 48 px target.
The control is visible and meaningful when the icon asset fails.
Heading hierarchy remains correct on every page using the component.
At user text-spacing overrides, nothing clips or overlaps.
The introduction can be understood without the decorative eyebrow.
Every card has one understandable destination and no nested interactive elements.
Longest FI and EN headings fit at 320 px and 200% text.
Text remains selectable; the click layer does not steal adjacent actions.
Default, hover, focus and touch screenshots preserve consistent depth.
At 20, 24 and 32 px the icon family has consistent visual weight.
Screen readers do not announce redundant decorative numbers and symbols.
The service order is identical between card grid, service selector and contact field.
Visitors can distinguish a demonstration from client work without opening a disclaimer.
Before/After works with keyboard, touch and reduced motion.
The figure has an accessible explanation of the same substantive outcome.
No backing plane or shadow covers a link, caption or focus outline.
A first-time reader correctly identifies the item's evidence category.
Grayscale and screen-reader versions retain the distinction.
Every published Client work label has a linked internal permission record.
Every number can be traced to an approved evidence record.
A visitor can tell whether a figure is historical, illustrative or a target.
The same value is announced by assistive technology and displayed visually.
Every item has an accessible title, useful image alternative and correct content-type label.
Card click and title-link destinations match.
No personal/customer information is exposed in screenshots, thumbnails or metadata.
All six services can be selected with keyboard and no pointer.
Selected state, focused state and panel label are independently correct.
A copied service URL opens the intended service in both languages.
Back/Forward and invalid service slugs produce a predictable accessible state.
Each service displays its correct tasks, deliverables, limits and contact topic.
No heading level is skipped solely because the component is reused.
The longest translated panel fits with text-spacing overrides.
Selecting a service does not create repeated noisy live announcements.
Sequence remains clear when CSS decoration is removed.
Text uses factual outputs rather than unverifiable promises.
At mobile widths the reading order remains 01 through 04.
The notice can be found before an enquiry without dominating the initial service explanation.
FI and EN versions impose the same scope boundaries.
Screen readers encounter the notice naturally, without an unnecessary interruption.
Every published quote exactly matches its approved wording and attribution.
Permission covers website and competition-submission use.
The page remains well composed when no testimonial is available.
Business identity and service claims match approved company information.
The visitor understands current capabilities without mistaking future plans for available services.
All personal information and portraits have publication permission.
The pictured person and the published identity match the authorized source.
At all crops the face is not cut awkwardly or distorted.
The biography has owner approval and does not contain unverified credentials.
The CTA destination and optional service topic are correct.
The section remains readable at 320 px and enlarged text.
No unverified response-time or outcome promise appears in the copy.
All footer links resolve correctly in FI and EN.
The original logo colors remain intact.
A visitor can find the privacy notice and operational contact fallback from any page.
Mobile footer spacing and contrast remain comfortable at enlarged text.
A real synthetic test enquiry reaches the controlled receiving mailbox before release.
Blank required fields and malformed email produce helpful localized feedback.
Form can be completed by keyboard and assistive technology.
Blocked scripts or a failed mail service leave an honest recovery path.
Test Finnish diacritics, multi-part names, apostrophes and non-Latin names through appropriate fallback rendering.
An empty name does not block a valid enquiry.
The field label and any error are programmatically associated.
Valid plus-addressed and long-domain email examples are accepted.
Malformed input gets a localized, associated error without clearing other fields.
Header-control characters are rejected safely by server validation.
Mobile keyboards expose an appropriate email-entry layout.
Every service-specific contact link prefills the matching service.
Keyboard and mobile-native selection work without custom gesture requirements.
A malformed query value cannot inject markup or alter the form structure.
The visible and submitted option correspond in both locales.
Long Finnish text, line breaks and pasted plain text remain readable and preserved after an error.
Whitespace-only input is rejected with a useful explanation.
Maximum-length behavior is identical in client and server intent; no silent content loss.
Text-area resize does not cover the submit control.
The note describes the actual deployed data flow.
There is no bundled or preselected marketing permission.
Privacy link is operable and form content is not accidentally lost when reviewing it.
Submitting multiple invalid fields moves focus to a summary that lists all actionable errors.
Each summary link reaches the correct input and its label/error is announced.
Correcting one field does not erase another field's value.
Errors are understandable without red color.
Every invalid control has a readable associated repair message.
No duplicate announcement storm occurs on submit.
At large text and narrow widths messages expand cleanly beneath inputs.
Rapid double-click and Enter repetition create one accepted enquiry.
Slow-network state acknowledges submission without moving the layout.
Timeout produces an honest recovery message and preserves fields.
Reduced-motion mode does not display an endlessly animated spinner.
A simulated rejected server request never shows success.
Success wording matches whether the backend accepted, queued or actually sent the enquiry.
Focus and announcement communicate completion without requiring sight.
No personal message content appears in URL, logs or telemetry.
Simulate 400, 429, 500, offline and timeout responses and verify distinct truthful behavior.
All typed content survives recoverable failures.
Recovery does not duplicate an already accepted request.
The fallback address is real, operational and consistently branded where approved.
Image failure does not collapse the layout or remove the substantive explanation.
Captions stay visually associated with their figures at all widths.
All credits and permissions match the asset register.
A screen-reader user receives the same essential information as a visual reader.
The text equivalent contains the same sequence, relationships and values.
Diagram remains legible at phone width without shrinking all labels.
Color-blind and grayscale views preserve distinctions through labels/shapes.
All displayed data is real and approved or explicitly synthetic.
A screen reader associates values with the correct row/column headers.
At 320 px the local scroll area is usable without causing page-wide horizontal scrolling.
All figures have defined units and evidence.
Printed output retains table meaning and column labels.
Enter and Space operate the heading and its expanded state is announced.
Links in a closed panel are not focusable; open links are reachable.
Long answers and text-spacing overrides do not clip.
Core contact/service information remains understandable without opening FAQs.
A copied fragment URL lands on the correct visible heading.
Keyboard activation moves to a logical reading position.
Reduced-motion mode has no animated scrolling.
The link never covers another control on phones.
File opens/downloads correctly and the stated size, format and language match.
Equivalent essential information remains available as HTML.
The document has its own accessibility and content approval.
Opening, keyboard cycling, Escape and close restoration match the modal contract.
At 400% zoom the entire dialog remains reachable without losing its close control.
A route transition while open removes backdrop, inert state and scroll lock.
No modal appears unsolicited during the primary business journey.
No essential information exists only in a disappearing notification.
Screen-reader announcement is polite and does not interrupt typing.
The notice never covers the video control or submit action on a phone.
Empty and unavailable states have a clear recovery action.
No fake content is inserted to satisfy a visual grid.
Keyboard focus remains predictable after clearing filters.
Slow network does not hide the primary proposition or Contact link.
Asset failure resolves to a stable fallback rather than an endless skeleton.
Measured layout shifts remain within the project budget.
Reduced motion removes nonessential loading animation.
A deliberately nonexistent URL returns 404 with the branded usable page.
All recovery links work and preserve language.
The page is keyboard-usable, readable in both themes and not indexed as normal content.
Simulated server failure leaves an intelligible, accessible fallback.
No sensitive system details appear in the response.
Retry cannot create duplicate enquiry side effects.
The fallback works when the main application bundle fails.
Network loss during typing preserves the visible draft.
Network loss during sending does not show false success.
Reconnection does not silently duplicate a message or reveal stored personal data.
Before an optional consent choice, network/storage inspection finds no optional tracker activity.
Reject and withdrawal actually stop the corresponding processing.
The interface is usable without deceptive button hierarchy.
Privacy owner approves the deployed behavior and notice together.
Each route family has a legible, localized preview rather than a duplicated generic card.
Preview metadata URLs resolve publicly and use the canonical host.
Text remains within safe areas under common preview crops.
Tab, pinned shortcut and mobile touch icon render the approved brand mark.
All route titles distinguish the actual page and language.
No broken icon request or framework-default identity remains.
A full-page overview shows a coherent surface rhythm without visual clutter.
No section background undermines text or focus contrast.
Breakpoints do not create unintended seams, gaps or clipped shadows.
Home, service detail and privacy print previews preserve all essential meaning.
No clipped text, white-on-white headings or overlapping fixed header appears.
Printed examples retain their demonstration/client-work labels.
Every public accessibility claim is supported by a current scoped review.
The feedback route works without inaccessible prerequisites.
Known limitations are understandable and match the release issue register.
